A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoLoR research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–B are readable, and retained equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and compression experiments, ablations, manual evaluations, positional analyses, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds single-domain transfer experiments and compression-time measurements in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The preference-pair construction, length-weighted ORPO objective, passage compression, and LCLM retrieval procedure are unchanged. Newly naming the synthetic-data generators provides implementation documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine main datasets, ArguAna and Touché-2020, and the appendix long-context datasets. The added transfer experiments restrict training to existing domains without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in retained experiments. The new transfer comparison reuses Raw Passage and Comp. w/ Phi, while the timing comparison reuses Phi and COMPACT; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: V2 adds training restricted to either fact-checking or multi-document datasets followed by cross-domain evaluation (Table 3), and FIQA corpus-compression timing under a stated same-hardware control (Table 4). Existing training settings, splits, retrieval metrics, and prompting protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends domain-generalization testing with single-domain training and adds a focused analysis of compression overhead. Existing loss ablations, base-model comparisons, passage-position tests, manual fact evaluation, and the appendix case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All matched pre-existing numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. V2 adds transfer results (Table 3), FIQA compression times of 1290.82 seconds for CoLoR, 1485.63 for Phi, and 3473.95 for COMPACT (Table 4), and passage-length summaries (Table 10).

T1.justification: The retrieval definitions, compressed-corpus formulation, ORPO loss, length-weighted CoLoR objective, and associated mathematical assumptions are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task-specific compression contribution and headline claims of 6% better retrieval and 1.91-fold context compression. The new experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The new compression-process discussion attributes COMPACT's longer runtime to iterative compression and characterizes CoLoR's preprocessing burden as small. Existing limitations and interpretations concerning information retention, passage position, and conventional retrieval are unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a CoLoR code link, names four synthetic-data generators, explicitly documents the zero-shot compression prompt, and supplies benchmark corpus sizes and passage-length statistics in Appendix A. Existing hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and training/validation counts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Mistral 7B and The Llama 3 Herd of Models while retaining the same research positioning. It removes Ni et al.'s Sentence-T5 reference and instead cites a duplicate Sentence-BERT entry for SentenceT5. Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language and cross-reference edits, moves manual evaluation to the end of Section 5, expands Appendix A, and adds acknowledgements. The overall section organization and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables for transfer results, compression costs, and corpus statistics. It enlarges and relocates Figures 3–4, reformats the out-of-domain table, and widens the conventional-retrieval table. All five figures retain their underlying graphical content.

improvement.justification: The added transfer and compression-time experiments provide useful support for the existing claims, while generator identities, corpus statistics, and the code link improve reproducibility information. These focused gains outweigh the new Sentence-T5 citation error. The improvement remains limited: timing evidence covers only FIQA preprocessing, and the original method and benchmark results are unchanged.
